datasets.title: Tomorrow's Cities Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment Dataset for Quito (Santa Rosa), Ecuador
datasets.description: Multi-hazard risk data package for Santa Rosa district, Quito, Ecuador, providing earthquake hazard (2 PGA scenarios as XLSX grid data), debris flow hazard (1 depth scenario), flood vulnerability functions (no flood depth data), synthetic future urban exposure datasets (buildings, households, land use) for three community planning scenarios (VS0, VS2, VS3), and multi-hazard impact assessment results. Developed as part of the Tomorrow's Cities GCRF Urban Disaster Risk Hub project for risk-informed decision making in urban planning.
datasets.purpose: To support multi-hazard risk assessment and risk-informed urban planning decision making for Quito (Santa Rosa district) by providing spatial hazard, synthetic future exposure, vulnerability/fragility functions, and impact assessment datasets for participatory community planning scenarios.

project.name: Tomorrow's Cities - GCRF Urban Disaster Risk Hub

datasets.details: The dataset includes: (i) earthquake hazard as 2 XLSX PGA scenario grids (EQ-SCEN1-PGA.xlsx, EQ-SCEN2-PGA.xlsx) with 499 points providing X/Y projected coordinates and IM (PGA in g), earthquake fragility for 11 building typologies (5 damage states DS1-DS5 with SA intensity measure and period-dependent parameters), debris flow fragility for 11 typologies; (ii) debris flow depth scenario (DF-SCEN01-DPTH.xlsx, 3.0 MB) with depth values; (iii) flood vulnerability functions for 1,260 building typologies at 9 water depths (0-6m) - note: no flood depth hazard map provided, flood assessed through debris flow depth proxy; (iv) three future exposure dataset variants (VS0: Santa Rosa baseline, VS2: Vision 2, VS3: Vision 3; VS1 absent) each containing building footprints (333 buildings) with structural taxonomy, household data (497 households), and land use plans (6 zones, 2 residential types); and (v) multi-hazard impact results including metrics.txt summary files with damage distribution and impact metrics (metric3-metric8) for both basic (v1) and enhanced (v2) analysis versions.

contact_point.name: Menteşe, E.Y. - Anofa Engineering, Planning and Informatics Ltd.

sources.name: Building footprints and exposure data
sources.description: Building footprints with structural taxonomy for Santa Rosa district, Quito. Only 333 buildings across 6 land use zones - smallest exposure dataset of all Tomorrow's Cities. Lineage: Building data with camelCase field names (zoneID, nHouse, expStr, bldID, repValue, fptarea, residents). Typology includes Adobe (Adb+LC+LR), RC infilled, and Brick masonry structures.

sources.name: Synthetic population generation algorithm
sources.description: Bespoke algorithms developed to generate synthetic future population (households) based on population projections and land use plans through participatory community engagement. Lineage: Algorithms coded in MATLAB environment to produce synthetic social data representing future urban scenarios. Methodology described in Menteşe et al. (2023).

sources.name: Earthquake hazard scenarios
sources.description: Two earthquake PGA scenarios (EQ-SCEN1 and EQ-SCEN2) provided as XLSX grids with 499 points per scenario, with X/Y projected coordinates and IM (PGA in g). All hazard data is tabular - no GeoTIFF or GeoJSON rasters. Lineage: Generated for Santa Rosa district, Quito. Source fault, magnitude, and depth parameters not documented.

sources.name: Debris flow depth scenario
sources.description: Single debris flow depth scenario (DF-SCEN01-DPTH.xlsx, 3.0 MB) providing depth values for the Santa Rosa study area. Lineage: Debris flow simulation for Santa Rosa area. Return period, trigger mechanism, and volume not documented.

sources.name: Earthquake fragility functions
sources.description: Fragility functions for 11 building typologies defining probability of exceeding 5 damage states (DS1-DS5) as a function of spectral acceleration, with period-dependent parameters. Typologies include Adobe (Adb+LC+LR), RC infilled, Brick masonry. Lineage: Developed based on consultation with local partners and global vulnerability databases.

sources.name: Debris flow fragility functions
sources.description: Fragility functions for 11 building typologies (same format as flood vulnerability) defining damage ratios at debris/water depths from hw0 to hw6. Lineage: Developed based on consultation with local partners.

sources.name: Flood vulnerability functions
sources.description: Depth-damage vulnerability functions defining damage ratio as a function of water depth for 1,260 building typologies at 9 water depth levels (0-6m). Note: No flood depth hazard map provided - flood is assessed through debris flow depth proxy. Lineage: Produced based on consultation with local partners and global vulnerability databases.

lineage.description: Integrated multi-hazard risk dataset produced by the Tomorrow's Cities GCRF Urban Disaster Risk Hub. OpenStreetMap building footprints were classified by construction type, occupancy, and number of storeys and enriched with replacement value estimates. A synthetic population was generated from census data using the agent-based algorithm of Calderon and Silva (2023, doi:10.1016/j.ijdrr.2023.103651), disaggregating individuals to buildings via household composition models. Earthquake hazard scenarios were simulated using OpenQuake-based GMPE ensembles (Weatherill et al. 2022). Flood hazard maps were derived from NASADEM-based hydrodynamic modelling. Earthquake building fragility functions and road/infrastructure fragility functions were adapted from HAZUS guidelines; flood depth-damage vulnerability functions from the JRC European flood damage database.

resources.title: Quito Multi Hazard Dataset
resources.description: Multi-hazard dataset containing: (1) 2 earthquake PGA scenario XLSX grids (499 points each); (2) 1 debris flow depth scenario XLSX (3.0 MB); (3) Earthquake fragility for 11 typologies (DS1-DS5); (4) Debris flow fragility for 11 typologies; (5) Flood vulnerability for 1,260 typologies (no flood depth data provided). All hazard data is tabular (XLSX), not raster.

resources.title: Quito Future Exposure Dataset - VS0
resources.description: Future urban exposure dataset for VS0 (Santa Rosa baseline), including building footprints (333 buildings) with structural taxonomy, household data (497 households), and land use plan (6 zones). Data formats: Shapefile for spatial data, Excel (XLSX) for tabular data. No individual-level data.

events.description: Earthquake Scenario 1 for Santa Rosa area providing Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) values at 499 grid points. Tabular XLSX format with X/Y projected coordinates and IM values. File: EQ-SCEN1-PGA.xlsx
Earthquake Scenario 2 for Santa Rosa area providing Peak Ground Acceleration (PGA) values at 499 grid points. File: EQ-SCEN2-PGA.xlsx
Debris flow Scenario 01 for Santa Rosa area providing depth values. Tabular XLSX format (3.0 MB). Also serves as proxy for flood hazard assessment. File: DF-SCEN01-DPTH.xlsx

deterministic.index_criteria: Scenario-based deterministic analysis - return period and trigger mechanism undocumented

asset_type.title: Building taxonomy
asset_type.description: Building exposure classified using the GEM Global Exposure Database for All (GED4ALL) taxonomy, sourced from OpenStreetMap building footprints

asset_type.title: Population exposure model
asset_type.description: Synthetic population derived from census household data using the Tomorrow's Cities DST population generation algorithm

asset_type.title: Land use exposure
asset_type.description: Urban land use classification areas classified per GED4ALL exposure framework

vulnerability.analysis_details: Depth-damage vulnerability functions defining damage ratio as a function of water depth (0-6m at 9 discrete levels) for 1,260 building typologies. Note: No flood depth hazard map provided - flood is assessed through debris flow depth proxy.
Debris flow depth-damage vulnerability functions for 11 building typologies defining damage ratios at debris depths from hw0 to hw6 (same format as flood vulnerability).

fragility.analysis_details: Lognormal fragility functions for 11 building typologies defining probability of exceeding 5 damage states (DS1-DS5) as a function of spectral acceleration (g). Period-dependent parameters (periodMin, periodMax). Typologies include Adobe (Adb+LC+LR), RC infilled, Brick masonry with various code levels.

socio_economic.description: Income level attribute for synthetic households used as socio-economic indicator in the exposure dataset.

losses.description: Building damage state results from earthquake impact assessment for each vision scenario (VS0, VS2, VS3) and both earthquake scenarios (SCEN1, SCEN2), with basic (v1) and enhanced (v2) analysis versions.
Building damage state results from debris flow impact assessment for each vision scenario.

Affected population metrics from multi-hazard impact assessment including homeless households/individuals (metric5/metric6), hospital access disruption (metric3/metric4), and total reposition value for damaged buildings (metric8).
